main.claim: Open the voice recorder, allow microphone access, and press Record. A timer and a level meter show that your mic is picking up your voice. Pause and resume, play it back, then download it. Free, no app, nothing uploaded.

sections.heading: How to record your voice online
sections.body:
The recorder runs in your browser, so there is nothing to install. Open it in the browser you already use, then select Allow when the browser asks for the microphone. If you blocked the prompt earlier, allow the microphone in the site settings and reload the page.

1. Open the [voice recorder](https://voice-recorder.lazur.app/).
2. Select Allow for the microphone.
3. Press Record and speak. The timer starts at 00:00 and the level meter moves with your voice.
4. Press Pause when you need a break, then Resume to keep going.
5. Stop the recording, press Play to listen, then download it.

**Check the meter before you start.** If it stays flat while you speak, the page is not getting sound from your mic yet. Choose the right input in your computer's sound settings, then record a few seconds to test.

sections.heading: What you get when you download
sections.body:
The download is the recording exactly as your browser saved it. Depending on the browser, that is WebM, OGG or MP4. The recorder does not choose the format for you, so the file type can differ from one browser to another.

Play the file before you rely on it. If you plan to edit it, check that your editor opens that file type. If it does not, convert the file with a free converter and keep the original as a backup.

sections.heading: The live transcript
sections.body:
When your browser supports speech recognition, a transcript appears next to the recording while you talk. It is useful for notes, a rough script or a quick check of what you said.

**Treat the transcript as a draft.** Speech recognition misses words, especially names, numbers and fast speech. Listen to the recording and correct the text before you share it.

Speech recognition runs in your browser's own speech service, not in this page. On some browsers, that service handles the audio on a remote server, so read the next section before you use the transcript for private material.

sections.heading: Where your recording stays
sections.body:
Lazur does not upload your recording. The audio stays in the browser tab while you work, and you choose whether to download it. The transcript is the one part that depends on your browser. Some browsers send the audio for speech recognition to a web service, so keep that in mind for anything confidential.

For a recording you do not want a service to read, skip the live transcript and record without it. For a full step-by-step on each device, see the [voice recorder pages](https://voice-recorder.lazur.app/record) for your computer, phone or use case.

pages.description: Record your voice on a Windows PC in your browser. Allow the mic, watch the level meter, pause, play back and download. Free, no app to install.
pages.claim: Open the recorder in your browser on your PC, allow the microphone, and press Record. The timer and level meter show your mic is working. Pause, play back, then download the recording. Free, no install needed.

sections.heading: Allow the microphone in Windows 11
sections.body:
Before the browser can use your mic, Windows has to allow it. Microsoft's steps for Windows 11 are these.

1. Select Start, then Settings, then Privacy & security.
2. Under App permissions, select Microphone.
3. Make sure Microphone access is on.
4. Make sure Let apps access your microphone is On.
5. Under Choose which apps can access your microphone, turn on Let desktop apps access your microphone.

The last switch matters for Chrome, Edge and Firefox, because they are desktop apps. If it is off, the browser cannot hear your mic even when the page asks. Microsoft's full guide is [Turn on app permissions for your microphone in Windows](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/privacy/turn-on-app-permissions-for-your-microphone-in-windows).

sections.heading: Record in the browser
sections.body:
Open the [voice recorder](https://voice-recorder.lazur.app/pc) in the browser you use every day. Select Allow when the page asks for the microphone, then press Record.

The timer runs from 00:00, and the level meter moves when your mic picks up sound. Use Pause to stop for a moment and Resume to carry on. When you are done, stop the recording, press Play to listen, and download it.

If you have a headset and a built-in mic, Windows may use the one you did not expect. Pick the input you want under Settings, then System, then Sound, in the Input section, and record a few seconds before you start the real take.

sections.heading: If the meter stays flat
sections.body:
A flat meter means the page is not getting sound. Check these in order. First, make sure the mic is plugged in or turned on, and that Windows lists it in the Input section. Second, close any other app that might be using the mic, such as a call app or a recorder. Third, reload the page and allow the microphone again.

If the meter still does not move, try the same mic in another app. If that app records sound, the problem is most likely the browser's permission, not the mic.

If the other app fails too, the device or its connection is the likely cause. Unplug a USB mic and plug it into another port, or try a headset with a cable you know works. Then open the recorder again and test once more before you assume the mic is broken.

sections.heading: Save the file on your PC
sections.body:
When you download, the file goes to your browser's download folder. The format depends on the browser: WebM, OGG or MP4. Open the file in a media player to check the sound before you use it.

If you plan to use the file in another program, check that the program opens that format. A converter can change the format if it does not.

faq.q: How do I record audio on my PC for free?
faq.a: Open the voice recorder in your browser, select Allow for the microphone, and press Record. Stop when you are done, press Play to listen, and download the file. There is nothing to install and no sign-up is needed.

faq.q: Why won't my PC browser record my voice?
faq.a: Usually Windows or the browser is blocking the microphone. In Windows 11, check Microphone access and Let desktop apps access your microphone under Privacy & security. Then allow the mic in the browser, reload the page and record again.

faq.q: What file type does the recording download as?
faq.a: It depends on the browser. The recorder saves whatever format your browser makes, which is usually WebM, OGG or MP4. Play the file to check it, and convert it if the program you use cannot open it.

pages.description: Record a voiceover for a YouTube video in your browser. Pause, listen back, then download the audio for your editor. Free, no sign-up needed.
pages.claim: Record your voiceover in the browser: allow the mic, press Record, pause while you read your script, then play it back and download the audio. The file goes into your video editor, not onto YouTube. Free, no sign-up.

sections.heading: What the recorder does for a YouTube video
sections.body:
This recorder captures your voice from the microphone and saves it as a file. It does not edit video and it does not connect to YouTube. You record the voiceover here, download it, and add it to the project in your video editor.

That split keeps the job simple. The recorder handles the voice, and your editor handles the timing, music and picture.

sections.heading: Record a voiceover step by step
sections.body:
1. Open the [voice recorder](https://voice-recorder.lazur.app/youtube) and select Allow when the browser asks for the microphone.
2. Read your script once without recording, so you know where the breaks fall.
3. Press Record, then read one section at a time.
4. Press Pause between sections, then Resume when you are ready.
5. Stop the recording, press Play, and listen for stumbles or noise.
6. Download the file.

Record each section as its own take if you want to re-do one part later. Keep a note of the take number, because a single long file is harder to fix than several short ones.

**Keep the mic at the same distance for every take.** A change in distance changes the volume, and that is hard to fix later.

sections.heading: Clean up the sound before you upload
sections.body:
A voiceover shows every noise, so record in a quiet room. Turn off fans and close windows if you can. Keep a soft surface around you, such as a rug or curtains, to reduce echo.

Listen with headphones while you play back the take. Speakers can send sound back into the mic. If the words are clear and the volume is steady, the take is ready for your editor.

If a take has a hum, a click from a keyboard or a car going past, record it again rather than trying to fix it later. Noise removal in an editor can make a voice sound thin, so a clean take is almost always the better choice. Read the sentence slowly once more, sit in the same spot, and record that section again.

sections.heading: Bring the file into your editor
sections.body:
Most editors accept MP4 and WebM files, and many accept audio directly. Drop the downloaded file into your project, place it on the audio track, then trim the start and end. If your editor will not open the file, convert it to a common format first and keep the original.

Line the voiceover up with the picture once the whole narration is in place, not piece by piece. Then listen to the full track at normal speed. Pauses that felt right while you were recording can feel long on screen, so shorten them where the video needs a faster pace. Keep the original take files in a folder next to the project, so you can swap in a better take later without recording again.

YouTube's own help center explains how to upload a finished video, including the audio in it. This recorder only makes the voice file.

faq.q: Can I record a voiceover for YouTube online?
faq.a: Yes. Open the voice recorder in your browser, allow the microphone, and press Record. Pause between sections, play back the take, and download the file. You then add it to your video in your editor.

faq.q: Can I record audio from YouTube with this tool?
faq.a: No. This recorder captures sound from your microphone, not from a YouTube video playing on your screen. To record your own voiceover, read your script into the microphone and download the take.

faq.q: What is the best way to record a YouTube voiceover?
faq.a: Use a quiet room, keep the mic at the same distance, and record each section as its own take. Play each take back with headphones before you move on, so you can re-record a weak section right away.

pages.title: Is an Online Voice Recorder Safe? What to Know | Lazur
pages.description: Find out whether this online voice recorder is safe to use. What stays in your browser, what the live transcript sends, and how to protect private recordings.
pages.h1: Is an online voice recorder safe?
pages.claim: Yes, for most recordings. Lazur does not upload your audio, and it stays in your browser until you download it. The one exception is the live transcript, which depends on your browser's speech service. Skip it for private material.

sections.heading: What stays on your device
sections.body:
This recorder runs in your browser. It uses your microphone to make the recording, and Lazur does not upload that recording. The audio stays in the page while you record, pause and play it back. When you download it, the file goes to your device, and what happens next is up to you.

The recorder asks for microphone access before it can start. That is the browser's standard permission, and you can take it back in your browser's site settings at any time.

sections.heading: The live transcript is the exception
sections.body:
The live transcript uses speech recognition that your browser provides. The Mozilla Developer Network notes that on some browsers, speech recognition uses a server-based engine by default, and the audio is sent to a web service to be processed. That is the browser's service, not Lazur's.

If a recording is private, such as a client call, a medical note or a personal letter, do not use the live transcript. Record without it, and use your own offline tools for any transcription you need.

sections.heading: Protect a recording you care about
sections.body:
Before you record anything sensitive, check three things. Make sure no one else can see your screen or hear the room. Close other tabs and apps that could record your screen or sound. Download the file to a folder you control, and move it somewhere protected if it contains private information.

Remember that a download is a copy on your device. Anyone with access to that device, or to a cloud sync folder, can open the file.

If you save recordings to a cloud sync folder such as OneDrive or Google Drive, the sync app may upload the file for you. That step is separate from this recorder, so check the sync settings before you put a private recording in a synced folder. Keep sensitive files in a local folder you control, and delete copies you no longer need.

Finally, think about who is in the room. A recording can pick up other people's voices, a phone call on speaker or a screen with names on it. Ask for consent before you record someone else, and check the rules that apply where you live.

sections.heading: When an online recorder is a good choice
sections.body:
For a quick note, a practice take or a voice sample you will share on purpose, a browser recorder is simple and needs no install. For anything with legal or medical weight, use a tool that you have checked and that fits your rules, such as one your organization approves.

When you are unsure, record a short test first and listen to it. You can see for yourself what the file contains before you rely on it.

faq.q: Is an online voice recorder safe to use?
faq.a: For most recordings, yes. This recorder keeps the audio in your browser and Lazur does not upload it. The live transcript is the exception, because some browsers send audio to a speech service. Skip the transcript for anything private.

faq.q: Does the voice recorder upload my recordings?
faq.a: Lazur does not upload your recording. It stays in your browser while you record and play it back, and it is saved only when you download it. The live transcript runs on your browser's speech service, which can process audio on a server.

faq.q: Can someone record my voice without me knowing?
faq.a: Anyone with access to your device or microphone can record you. A web page only records when you allow the microphone and press Record. Check the browser's site settings and close tabs you do not recognize if you are worried.

pages.description: Learn how to record on a voice recorder in your browser: allow the mic, press Record, pause, play back and download. Free, with steps for a computer.
pages.h1: How to record on a voice recorder
pages.claim: Open the voice recorder, select Allow for the microphone, and press Record. Pause and resume as needed, then stop and press Play to listen. Download the file when it sounds right. Free, no app needed.

sections.heading: Record in four steps
sections.body:
1. Open the [voice recorder](https://voice-recorder.lazur.app/record) in your browser.
2. Select Allow when the browser asks for the microphone.
3. Press Record. The timer starts at 00:00, and the level meter moves when you speak.
4. Press Stop when you finish, then Play to check the take.

You can pause in the middle with Pause and start again with Resume. The recording continues from where you stopped, so you do not need a new file for each break.

A good first take is short. Record two or three sentences, play them back, and decide whether the voice, the volume and the room sound right. Only then record the full take. This takes less than a minute and saves you from re-doing a long recording after you find a problem at the end.

sections.heading: Check the level before you record
sections.body:
Speak at your normal volume and watch the meter. It should rise when you talk and fall when you stop. If it stays flat, the page is not getting sound from your microphone. Choose the mic you want in your computer's sound settings, close other apps that use it, and try again.

If the meter moves but the playback is quiet, move closer to the mic or raise the input level in your sound settings. Then record a short test and play it back.

sections.heading: Save the recording
sections.body:
Press Play to listen to the whole take. If it is right, download it. Your browser saves the file to its download folder. The format is WebM, OGG or MP4, depending on the browser.

Keep the original file until you have checked it in the program where you will use it.

Give the file a clear name when you save it, such as the date and the topic, so you can find it later. A name like recording1 is easy to lose among downloads. If you record several takes in one day, number them in the order you made them.

After you download, play the file from the folder where it was saved, not from the browser. That confirms the file is complete. If it plays silently or stops early, record again and download once more.

sections.heading: This is a browser recorder
sections.body: These steps cover the voice recorder in a web browser. The built-in voice recorder app on a phone, or a recorder app that came with your computer, works differently and has its own menus. For the built-in app on your device, check the manufacturer's own guide. If you only need a quick note on a computer, this browser recorder is often the faster option, because it needs no install and opens in a tab you already have.

faq.q: How do I record my voice on a computer?
faq.a: Open the voice recorder in your browser, select Allow for the microphone, and press Record. Stop when you are done, press Play to check the take, and download it. No install is needed.

faq.q: How do I pause a recording and continue?
faq.a: Press Pause to stop the recording for a moment. Press Resume to carry on. The take continues in the same file, so you do not need to start over after a break.

faq.q: Where does my recording go after I download it?
faq.a: It goes to your browser's download folder on your device. Lazur does not upload the recording. The file type is WebM, OGG or MP4, depending on your browser.

pages.title: Online Voice Recorder for Podcasts: Record Solo Free | Lazur
pages.description: Record a solo podcast intro or episode in your browser. Pause between takes, play back to check, and download the audio. Free, no sign-up needed.
pages.claim: Record a solo podcast in your browser: allow the mic, press Record, pause between takes, then play it back and download the audio. It records one microphone at a time, so it suits solo episodes, intros and voice notes. Free.

sections.heading: What it is good for
sections.body:
This recorder captures one microphone and saves the sound as a file. That makes it a good fit for a solo episode, a podcast intro, an outro, an ad read or a voice note for your show.

It records only the mic your computer is using, so use the same mic for every segment of an episode. It does not mix several people into one file. If you have a guest, record each person separately, or use a tool built for remote guests, and bring the tracks together in your editor.

sections.heading: Record an episode take by take
sections.body:
1. Open the [voice recorder](https://voice-recorder.lazur.app/podcast) and select Allow for the microphone.
2. Pick your mic if you have more than one, and speak at your normal volume.
3. Press Record, and read or talk through one segment.
4. Press Pause between segments, then Resume.
5. Stop, press Play to listen, and download the file.

Save each segment as its own take when you can. A short take is easier to re-do than a long one, and it is quicker to find the part you need in your editor.

Before you record a full episode, do a short test with the same mic, room and distance. Play it back with headphones. If the voice sounds thin, move slightly closer. If the words are hard to follow, check the input level in your sound settings. Keep your notes with the takes, so the next episode starts from the same setup.

sections.heading: Get a steady sound
sections.body:
Keep the mic the same distance from your mouth for the whole episode. Record in a room with soft furniture, and turn off fans and air conditioning if you can hear them. Listen with headphones so you hear what the mic hears, not the speakers.

If the level meter jumps or the recording clips, move a little farther from the mic and record a short test. The meter should rise and fall with your voice, not hit the top.

sections.heading: Use the download in your editor
sections.body:
The file is the take as your browser recorded it, in WebM, OGG or MP4. Open it in your editor to check that it loads, then trim the start and end and place the segments in order. If the editor will not open the file, convert it first and keep the original.

Add light edits only after the segments are in order. Remove long silences at the start and end, and check that each segment starts clean. Export a final mix, then listen to it on the device your listeners use most, such as a phone speaker or earbuds.

faq.q: Can I record a podcast with an online voice recorder?
faq.a: Yes, for a solo episode. Open the recorder, allow the microphone, and record your segments with Pause between them. Download each take and put them in order in your editor. For a guest, record each person separately.

faq.q: Can I record a podcast interview with a guest here?
faq.a: Not as one file. This recorder captures one microphone at a time. Record your own part here and your guest's part separately, then combine the tracks in your editor. A tool built for remote guests can record both people together.

faq.q: What format are podcast recordings saved in?
faq.a: The recorder saves what your browser produces, which is WebM, OGG or MP4. Most editors can import these files, but check yours first. If it cannot, convert the file and keep the original recording.
